Proxima Centauri: Robert T. A. Innes. Proxima Centauri is the nearest star to Earth after the Sun, located 4.25 light-years (1.3 parsecs) away in the southern constellation of Centaurus.
Who is credited with discovering Stirling's approximation?
Stirling's approximation: Abraham de Moivre. In mathematics, Stirling's approximation (or Stirling's formula) is an asymptotic approximation for factorials.
Who is credited with discovering Yttrium?
Yttrium: Johan Gadolin. Yttrium is a chemical element; it has symbol Y and atomic number 39.
This French surgeon won the 1912 Nobel for pioneering vascular suturing, then teamed up with aviator Charles Lindbergh to build the first perfusion pump for organ transplantation. Who was he?
Alexis Carrel (28 June 1873 - 5 November 1944) was a French surgeon and biologist who spent most of his scientific career in the United States.
Its scientific name translates roughly to 'fused lizard,' and it may be the largest of its armored kind at up to 8 tons — which dinosaur genus?
Ankylosaurus is a genus of armored dinosaur. It was named by Barnum Brown in 1908; it is monotypic, containing only A. magniventris.

Caused by the parasitic roundworm Ascaris lumbricoides, this infection hides in plain sight — over 85% of cases have no symptoms at all — yet in children it can stunt weight gain and trigger learning problems. What's the disease called?
Ascariasis is a disease caused by the parasitic roundworm Ascaris lumbricoides. The eggs hatch in the intestines, the larvae burrow through the gut wall, and migrate to the lungs via the blood.
This self-taught Maryland-born mathematician published a successful series of almanacs and assisted Major Andrew Ellicott in surveying the new federal capital district — who was he?
Benjamin Banneker (November 9, 1731 - October 19, 1806) was an American naturalist, mathematician, astronomer and almanac author.
With the formula B(OH)3 and found in nature as the mineral sassolite, this weak, water-soluble compound of boron serves as an antiseptic, insecticide, and flame retardant — which acid?
Boric acid is a compound of boron, oxygen, and hydrogen with formula B(OH)3.
The very same compound that hardens eggshells, builds pearls, and forms the chalk on a classroom board can also be swallowed as an antacid to calm an upset stomach — what is it?
Calcium carbonate is a chemical compound with the chemical formula CaCO3.
This usually bacterial infection of the skin's inner layers causes spreading redness, swelling, and pain, most often on the legs or face, sometimes accompanied by fever — what is it?
Cellulitis is usually a bacterial infection involving the inner layers of the skin. It specifically affects the dermis and subcutaneous fat.
This small, lean, mostly nocturnal mammal native to tropical Asia and Africa is often called a 'cat' in its common nickname, despite not actually being a cat at all — what is it?
Civet is a small, lean, mostly nocturnal mammal native to tropical Asia and Africa, especially the tropical forests.
Thanks to variations in the OR6A2 gene, some people taste this Mediterranean herb as fresh and citrusy while others swear it tastes like soap — its leaves are called cilantro in the US. What is it?
Coriander is an annual herb in the family Apiaceae.

Native to Madagascar and grown as an ornamental tree throughout the tropics, this legume species has fern-like leaves and a flamboyant summer display of orange-red flowers; its wild origin wasn't confirmed until 1932. What tree is this?
Delonix regia is a species of flowering plant in the bean family Fabaceae, subfamily Caesalpinioideae native to Madagascar.

Defined in humans as an adult height of 147 centimeters or less, this condition can be disproportionate (affecting limbs or torso alone) or proportionate, and typically comes with normal intelligence and near-normal life expectancy — which condition?
Dwarfism is a condition of people and animals marked by unusually small size or short stature.

Native only to a single island in French Polynesia, this arum-family plant is now one of the world's most popular houseplants, and an ecologically damaging invasive species from South Africa to the Pacific Islands. Name it?
Epipremnum aureum is a species in the arum family Araceae, native to Mo'orea in the Society Islands of French Polynesia.

Likely domesticated from the European polecat, with which it can still interbreed, this slender Mustelid pet weighs up to about two kilograms and comes in coats of black, brown or white — which animal?
Ferret (Mustela furo) is a small, domesticated species belonging to the family Mustelidae.

A bulbous Allium native to Central Asia and northeastern Iran, this kitchen staple counts the chive, leek, and shallot among its cousins and was prized by ancient Babylonians and Egyptians — what is it?
Garlic (Allium sativum) is a species of bulbous flowering plants in the genus Allium.
Bred for centuries to hunt by sight and speed rather than scent, this ancient dog breed's deep chest, flexible spine, and long legs make it one of the fastest breeds alive. Name the breed?
Greyhound is a breed of dog and a sighthound. It is an ancient breed historically developed for hunting game by sight and speed, and has later been used in organised coursing and greyhound racing.

This field of study concerns the methodological principles of interpretation — especially of biblical, philosophical, and wisdom texts — and has been broadly applied across law, history, and theology — what's it called?

Hermeneutics is the study of the methodological principles of interpretation, especially the interpretation of biblical texts, wisdom literature, and philosophical texts. As necessary, hermeneutics may include the art of understanding and communication.
Defined by Whipple's triad, this condition occurs when blood sugar falls below about 70 mg/dL, causing symptoms like headache, shakiness, confusion, and a fast heart rate — what's it called?

Hypoglycemia (American English), also spelled hypoglycaemia or hypoglycmia (British English), sometimes called low blood sugar, is a fall in blood sugar to levels below normal, typically below 70 mg/dL (3.9 mmol/L).
Known for the mantra 'Dying is not a crime,' this euthanasia advocate served eight years in prison after his fourth trial ended in a murder conviction — who is he?
Jack Kevorkian (May 26, 1928 - June 3, 2011), also known by the nickname "Dr.
Named after a 19th-century English physicist, this SI unit of energy equals the work done when a one-newton force moves an object one metre in the direction of that force — name the unit?
Joule (JOOL, or JOWL; symbol: J) is the unit of energy in the International System of Units (SI).
Native to the Mediterranean and prized for its fragrant purple blooms, this genus of some 47 flowering plant species belongs to the sage family — name it?
Lavandula (common name lavender) is a genus of 47 known species of perennial flowering plants in the sage family, Lamiaceae.
Descended from the YF-22 prototype, this supersonic air-superiority stealth fighter saw Boeing build its wings and aft fuselage while the prime contractor handled final assembly — what is it?
Lockheed Martin F-22 Raptor is an American twin-engine, jet-powered, all-weather, supersonic stealth fighter aircraft.

This psychiatric state of abnormally elevated energy and mood is sometimes called the mirror image of depression, though its heightened feelings can turn irritable or anxious just as easily as euphoric — what is it called?
Mania (also known as manic syndrome) is a psychiatric behavioral syndrome defined as a state of abnormally elevated arousal, affect, and energy level.
Used to treat cancers, autoimmune diseases like rheumatoid arthritis, and even ectopic pregnancies, this chemotherapy drug and immune suppressant can be taken either orally or by injection — name it?
Methotrexate is a chemotherapy agent and immune-system suppressant.
Containing antimicrobial lysozymes and immunoglobulins, most of this protective body fluid is produced in the gastrointestinal tract — what is it called?
Mucus is a slippery fluid produced by, and covering, mucous membranes.
Element 113, a synthetic and ferociously radioactive member of the periodic table, was confirmed by a team at Riken in Japan — what's its name?
Nihonium is a synthetic chemical element; it has symbol Nh and atomic number 113.
Listed by Ptolemy and named for a hunter in Greek myth, this winter constellation boasts the supergiant stars Rigel and Betelgeuse and a famous short, straight line of three stars — which is it?
Orion (constellation) is a prominent set of stars visible during winter in the northern celestial hemisphere.
About 3,000 varieties of this apple-like fruit exist worldwide, and its fermented juice is known as perry — which fruit is it?
Pear are a genus of trees, Pyrus, in the family Rosaceae, that bear an edible apple-like fruit of the same name.

This subdiscipline of biology examines how organisms, organs, cells, and biomolecules carry out their chemical and physical functions, and its name derives from Greek words for 'nature' and 'study of' — what is it?
Physiology (from Ancient Greek (phsis) 'nature, origin' and - (-loga) 'study of') is the scientific study of functions and mechanisms in a living system.
This chemical compound, known in nature as the mineral niter and historically as a form of saltpetre, is widely used in fertilizers. What is it?
Potassium nitrate is a chemical compound with a sharp, salty, bitter taste and the chemical formula KNO3.
Its common side effects read like a list of trade-offs — sedation, weight gain, dry mouth — yet many take this atypical antipsychotic simply to fall asleep — which medication?
Quetiapine (kwi-), sold under the brand name Seroquel among others, is an atypical antipsychotic medication used in the treatment of schizophrenia, bipolar disorder, and major depressive disorder.

This interdisciplinary field studies and practices the design, construction, and operation of robots, typically combining a power source, mechanical structure, control circuitry, and software — what's the field called?
Robotics is the interdisciplinary study and practice of the design, construction, operation, and use of robots.
Found on every continent but Antarctica and numbering over 2,500 species, this eight-legged arachnid curves a stinger-tipped tail over its back — what is it?

Scorpion (order Scorpiones) are predatory arachnids with eight legs, a pair of grasping pincers (or Chelae) and a narrow, segmented tail, often carried in a characteristic forward curve over the back and always ending with a stinger.
This mammal family is known for its warning coloration and its ability to blast predators with a pungent spray from its anal glands — which animal?
Skunk are mammals in the family Mephitidae.

After more than 40 years at DuPont, this Polish-American chemist became the first woman to win the company's Lavoisier Medal — an honor that recognized her invention of a famously bullet-stopping fiber. Who was she?
Stephanie Kwolek (July 31, 1923 - June 18, 2014) was a Polish-American chemist known for inventing Kevlar (poly-paraphenylene terephthalamide).
One of the oldest constellations, this zodiac figure once marked the Sun's place at the spring equinox and inspired bull imagery from Sumer to Rome — which northern-sky constellation is it?
Taurus (constellation) (Latin, 'Bull') is one of the constellations of the zodiac and is located in the northern celestial hemisphere.

A colorless, sweet-smelling liquid that helps give gasoline and paint fumes their aroma, this benzene relative — a methyl group on a phenyl ring — serves as paint thinner and industrial solvent. What is it?
Toluene is a substituted aromatic hydrocarbon with the chemical formula C6H5CH3, often abbreviated as PhCH3, where Ph stands for the phenyl group.

Constantly produced by cells lining the lower female reproductive tract, this fluid mixture of liquid, cells, and bacteria varies throughout the menstrual cycle and helps lubricate and protect the area — what is it called?
Vaginal discharge is a mixture of liquid, cells, and bacteria that lubricate and protect the vagina.
Caused by a mutation in the ATP7B gene, this inherited condition lets copper build up in the liver and brain, leading to tremors, personality changes, and yellowing skin — which condition?
Wilson's disease (also called hepatolenticular degeneration) is a genetic disorder characterized by the excess build-up of copper in the body.
Also known by his Latinized name Rhazes, this Persian polymath authored over 200 manuscripts on medicine, philosophy, and astronomy during the Islamic Golden Age — who was he?
Abu Bakr al-Razi: 10th-century Iranian physician and polymath.
Based on a civilian widebody jet, this European aerial-refueling tanker holds over 90% of the air-to-air refueling market outside the United States, with 17 countries as customers — which aircraft?

Airbus A330 MRTT: Aerial refuelling tanker aircraft. The Airbus A330 Multi Role Tanker Transport (MRTT) is a European aerial refueling and military transport aircraft based on the civilian Airbus A330.
Known in mineral form as gibbsite, this amphoteric white compound with the formula Al(OH)3 is a major component of the ore bauxite — what is it?
Aluminium hydroxide: Chemical compound. Aluminium hydroxide is amphoteric, meaning it has both basic and acidic properties.
Named for a modified fin ray it dangles like bait to lure in prey, this order of mostly bottom-dwelling creatures is known for extreme sexual dimorphism between the sexes — what are they called?
Anglerfish: Bony fish with a natural lure.
Nicknamed the 'Primeval Bird' in German, this magpie-sized, feathered dinosaur from 150-million-year-old Jurassic Germany was long hailed as the earliest known bird — what is it?
Archaeopteryx: Extinct genus of bird-like dinosaurs.
A cousin of the tomato and potato, this European nightshade is so toxic — via atropine and scopolamine — that even handling it can harm you; its other common name is "belladonna." What's the plant?
Atropa bella-donna: Deadly nightshade, a flowering plant.
Produced continuously from 1964 to 2021, this line of twin-turboprop utility aircraft outsold all of its turboprop rivals combined — which aircraft family?
Beechcraft King Air: Twin engine turboprop aircraft family. The King Air line comprises a number of twin-turboprop models that have been divided into two families.
Not a species of its own, it's really a melanistic leopard or jaguar whose rosettes are still hidden under the dark coat — what do we call this big-cat colour variant?
Black panther: Variant of leopard and jaguar. Black panthers of both species have excess black pigments, but their typical rosettes are also present.

Commonly known as mad cow disease, this fatal neurodegenerative illness in cattle is caused by a misfolded prion and can spread to humans as a variant of Creutzfeldt-Jakob disease. What is this cattle disease called?
Bovine spongiform encephalopathy: Fatal neurodegenerative disease of cattle. The United Kingdom was afflicted with an outbreak of BSE and vCJD in the 1980s and 1990s.
Designed in 1959 and partly based on Grace Hopper's FLOW-MATIC, this English-like programming language still runs mainframe banking systems today — what is it?
COBOL: Programming language with English-like syntax.
This medical emergency occurs when the heart suddenly stops beating effectively, cutting off blood flow to the brain and other organs within minutes — what is it called?
Cardiac arrest: Sudden or unexpected loss of heartbeat.
Latin for 'little brain,' this hindbrain structure fine-tunes motor coordination and timing without actually initiating movement — what is it?
Cerebellum: Structure at the rear of the vertebrate brain, beneath the cerebrum.

Caused by a bacterium spread through contaminated water and undercooked shellfish, this intestinal infection produces severe watery diarrhea that can trigger dehydration within hours — which disease is it?
Cholera: Bacterial infection of the small intestine.
Recognizable by a prominent crest and curved bill, this Australasian parrot family includes 21 species, the smallest of which is the cockatiel — which family of birds?
Cockatoo: Any bird in the family Cacatuidae.
These colonial marine invertebrates secrete calcium carbonate to build the hard skeletons that form tropical reefs — what are they?
Coral: Marine invertebrates of the subphylum Anthozoa.
Once sold under the brand name Flexeril and chemically similar to tricyclic antidepressants, this oral medication treats sudden muscle spasms — what's the drug?
Cyclobenzaprine: Muscle relaxant medication. It should not be used together with MAOIs.
Caused by about 40 types of fungus and often picked up in public showers or contact sports like wrestling, this infection produces a red, itchy, scaly circular rash — what is it?
Dermatophytosis: Fungus infection of the skin. Dermatophytosis, also known as tinea and ringworm, is a fungal infection of the skin (a dermatomycosis), that may affect skin, hair, and nails.
Brought to Australia as an infant, this geologist joined Shackleton's Nimrod Expedition and became a leading figure of the Heroic Age of Antarctic exploration — who is it?
Douglas Mawson: Australian geologist and explorer of the Antarctic (1882–1958)
This membrane-bound series of protein complexes shuttles electrons through redox reactions, building a proton gradient that ultimately powers the synthesis of ATP — what's it called?
Electron transport chain: Energy-producing metabolic pathway.
Named from the Greek for 'red skin,' this bacterial infection produces a raised, sharply defined, bright-red rash typically on the face or legs — what's the condition?
Erysipelas: Human disease from a bacterial infection of the skin.
Also nicknamed the 'baum' or 'sweet' variety, this mustelid species ranges across much of the continent into Asia Minor, the Caucasus, and parts of Iran, Iraq, and Syria. What animal is it?
European pine marten: Species of mammal in the mustelid family.

This branch of Islamic scholarship interprets the Quran and sunnah through jurist reasoning, producing fatwas — while sharia itself is seen as unchanging, this human field is considered fallible. What is it called?
Fiqh: Islamic jurisprudence. Thus, whereas sharia is considered immutable and infallible by Muslims, fiqh is considered fallible and changeable.
This cold-weather injury turns skin white or waxy-blue after tissue actually freezes, often preceded by a tingling, numb warning stage called frostnip — what is it?
Frostbite: Effect of low temperature on skin and other tissues.

Predicted by Mendeleev in 1869 under the placeholder name 'ekasilicon' and discovered in 1886 by Clemens Winkler, this metalloid element was named for its discoverer's home country — what element is it?
Germanium: Chemical element with atomic number 32 (Ge)
Born from an accidental 18th-century cross between the sweet orange and the pomelo in Barbados, this citrus hybrid is nicknamed the 'forbidden fruit.' What is it?
Grapefruit: Citrus fruit. The grapefruit (Citrus × paradisi) is a subtropical citrus tree known for its relatively large, sour to semi-sweet, somewhat bitter fruit.

This British aviation entrepreneur held three Guinness World Records after visiting the South Pole, the Challenger Deep, and space, then died in 2023 aboard the submersible that imploded near the Titanic wreck — who was he?
Also known as the cane spider or giant crab spider, this huntsman species native to the tropics has spread to subtropical regions worldwide — what is it?
Heteropoda venatoria: Species of spider. It is native to the tropical regions of the world, and it is present in some subtropical areas as an introduced species.
Marketed as Hydrodiuril, this medication treats high blood pressure and fluid retention by blocking sodium and chloride reabsorption in the kidneys' distal tubules — what drug is it?

Hydrochlorothiazide: Diuretic medication. Hydrochlorothiazide, sold under the brand name Hydrodiuril among others, is a diuretic medication used to treat hypertension and swelling due to fluid build-up.
First described to Europeans in 1812, this reddish-brown African antelope's males sport lyre-shaped horns up to three feet long — which animal?
Impala: Species of antelope found in Africa.
Appointed FBI director by Barack Obama in 2013, this former federal prosecutor was fired from the post in 2017 — who is he?
Back in 1859, this Irish physicist proved the link between atmospheric CO2 and what we now call the greenhouse effect — who was he?
A pastor's son and theoretical physicist, this man passed Manhattan Project secrets to the Soviets, served nine years in a British prison, then resumed his science career in East Germany. Who is he?
Klaus Fuchs: German-born British physicist and atomic spy (1911–1988)
Formulated in 1834, this principle of electromagnetism states that an induced current always flows in a direction that opposes the very change in magnetic field that created it — which principle?
Lenz's law: Electromagnetic opposition to change.

Born from a 1970s Skunk Works project to dodge Soviet missile defenses, this subsonic single-seat attack jet became the first operational aircraft ever designed around stealth technology, first flying in 1981 at Groom Lake — which aircraft is it?
Lockheed F-117 Nighthawk: American stealth ground-attack aircraft.
This age-related eye disease gradually damages the retina's central region, with a 'wet' form involving leaking blood vessels and a 'dry' form marked by deposits called drusen — what is it?
Macular degeneration: Vision loss due to damage to the macula of the eye.
Proposed by an American psychologist to explain what motivates human behaviour, this conceptualisation originally set out how many sets of basic needs?

Maslow's hierarchy of needs is a conceptualization of the needs or goals that motivate human behaviour, proposed by the American psychologist Abraham Maslow. In his original formulation there are five sets of basic needs.
In medicine, this term describes a disease spreading from a primary site to a secondary one — most often used for a cancer seeding new tumors elsewhere in the body — what is it?
Metastasis: Spreading of a disease inside a body. The newly pathological sites, then, are metastases (mets).
Sold as Remeron, this atypical tetracyclic antidepressant is often chosen when depression comes tangled with anxiety or insomnia — which drug is it?
Mirtazapine: Antidepressant medication. Mirtazapine, sold under the brand name Remeron among others, is an atypical tetracyclic antidepressant, and as such is used primarily to treat depression.
Serving as Turkey's minister overseeing environment and climate, who is set to preside over the 2026 UN Climate Change Conference, COP31?
A healthy kidney contains up to 1.5 million of these microscopic filtering units, each pairing a capillary tuft with a cup-shaped capsule — what is it called?
Nephron: Microscopic structural and functional unit of the kidney.
Represented by symbols like '11' in the Hindu-Arabic system used worldwide, these mathematical objects serve to count, measure, and label — what are they called?
Number: Used to count, measure, and label. The most basic examples are the natural numbers: 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, and so forth.
Described as far back as the 300s BC by Hippocrates, this bone infection most often strikes the spine in adults and the long bones in children — which condition?
Osteomyelitis: Infection of the bones. It may be acute or chronic and can be classified as hematogenous or non-hematogenous.
Also known as trisomy 13, this chromosomal condition arises when cells carry extra genetic material from chromosome 13, causing widespread organ defects — which syndrome?
Patau syndrome: Chromosomal disorder in which there are three copies of chromosome 13.
This legume's raw seeds contain a toxic compound that must be boiled away before eating, though its unripe green pods are eaten as-is — which species is it?

Derived in 1900 by a German physicist who proposed that an oscillator's energy could only change in discrete increments, this principle describes the spectral density of radiation from a black body at a given temperature — what is it called?
Planck's law: Spectral density of light emitted by a black body.
This common name describes small aquatic crustaceans with an exoskeleton and ten legs, especially popular in the UK and Commonwealth nations for larger swimming decapods — what is it?
Prawn: Common name applied to some types of crustaceans.
Ranging from Penguin Random House to countless small independent players, which broad industry covers making books, magazines, music, and software available to the public, in print or digital form?
Publishing: Production and distribution of media.

In a late stage of stellar evolution, this puffed-up, low-to-intermediate-mass star has a surface temperature around 5,000 K and burns helium or hydrogen in shells around its core — what type of star is it?
Red giant: Type of large cool star.
Also called a dassie, this small African and Middle Eastern mammal lives in crevice colonies of up to 80 and posts lookouts to warn of approaching predators — which animal?
Rock hyrax: Species of mammal native to Africa and the Middle East.
Dropped out of Stanford to co-found Loopt, later led Y Combinator, then became CEO of the company behind ChatGPT — briefly ousted by its board in 2023 for not being 'consistently candid.' Who is he?
Sam Altman: American entrepreneur and investor (born 1985)

Triggered when the body's own dysregulated response to infection starts damaging its tissues and organs, this life-threatening condition brings fever, rapid heartbeat, and confusion — which condition?

Sepsis: Life-threatening response to infection. Sepsis is a potentially life-threatening condition that arises when the body's dysregulated response to infection causes injury to its own tissues and organs.
Roughly 21 feet long yet coiled to fit inside the abdomen, this digestive tube receives bile and pancreatic juice and is divided into the duodenum, jejunum, and ileum — which organ?
Small intestine: Organ in the gastrointestinal tract.
Prized as the standard soundboard material for stringed instruments, this coniferous genus has four-sided needles and dominates boreal forests across the Northern Hemisphere — which tree genus?
Spruce: Genus of coniferous evergreen trees.
This tangy reddish spice, made from a shrub in the cashew family, is a staple of Arab cuisine and holds symbolic significance on the Haft-sin table at Persian New Year — what is it?
Sumac: Related species of plants in the family Anacardiaceae.
Prized for its durability and water resistance, this tropical hardwood with a leather-like smell when freshly milled is a top choice for boat building — what is it?
Teak: Tree species native to South and Southeast Asia.
Colored metallic blue on top and silvery below for camouflage, this genus of warm-blooded ocean fish includes the giant Atlantic bluefin and eight of the true tuna species — what genus is it?
Thunnus: Genus of fishes. Thunnus is a genus of ocean-dwelling, ray-finned bony fish from the mackerel family, Scombridae.
Named for its three heads — medial, lateral, and long — which upper-arm muscle straightens the elbow when it contracts?
Triceps: Muscle on the back of the upper arm. The triceps, or triceps brachii (Latin for "three-headed muscle of the arm"), is a large muscle on the back of the upper limb of many vertebrates.
Also known by the common names bilberry, blaeberry, and whortleberry, this holarctic shrub produces edible blue fruit — what is it?
Neither bee nor ant despite being closely related, yellowjackets and hornets belong to this narrow-waisted insect group that can deliver a painful sting — what is it?
Wasp: Group of insects. Unlike true parasites, the wasp larvae eventually kill their hosts.

Denied European certification after Russia's 2022 invasion of Ukraine, this single-aisle airliner made its maiden flight from Irkutsk in 2017 and is built by a UAC subsidiary of Rostec — which aircraft?
Yakovlev MC-21: Twin-engine Russian jet airliner.

The symbol for lithium is Li. Lithium is a chemical element; it has symbol Li and atomic number 3.

Julian Sands: Julian Richard Morley Sands (4 January 1958 – c. 13 January 2023) was an English actor.

Poor Things is a 2023 film directed by Yorgos Lanthimos and written by Tony McNamara, based on the 1992 novel by Alasdair Gray.

Tu Jhoothi Main Makkaar: The film stars Ranbir Kapoor and Shraddha Kapoor in the lead roles, alongside Dimple Kapadia, Boney Kapoor and Anubhav Singh Bassi in supporting roles.
In what year was No One Will Save You first released?
No One Will Save You: No One Will Save You is a 2023 American science fiction horror film written, directed, and co-produced by Brian Duffield.
In what year was Scandal first released?
Scandal is an American political thriller television series starring Kerry Washington.
In what year was The Legend of Tarzan first released?
The Legend of Tarzan is a 2016 action adventure film directed by David Yates.
In what year was American Made first released?
